bullets.title: NVDA crushes Q3, raises FY28 guidance to +75% YoY; stock +3-5% pre-market
bullets.body: NVDA reported Q3 revenue of $115.8B (+103% YoY, beat consensus ~$109B) and EPS of $2.68 (beat ~$2.48), with datacenter at $107.6B (+110% YoY). Q4 guidance midpoint $130B is ~4% above consensus; FY28 revenue growth guidance raised to ~75% from ~70%. Vera Rubin contributed ~$20B in its first quarter—fastest product ramp in company history—and total supply commitments rose to ~$390-430B from ~$279-311B, with >$100B tied to C2027 delivery.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO succession uncertainty and SEC probe are key overhangs post-earnings
bullets.body: The board confirmed it will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and is executing a formal search; interim CEO is CFO Colette Kress. An SEC civil probe into NVIDIA was separately disclosed, and the 10-Q filing has been delayed 'in coming weeks' due to an ongoing investigation. Jefferies noted 8 of 10 hedge fund investors spoken to in the past week hold a negative view, and retail dip-buying in NVDA has materially slowed. Wolfe cut its PT to $200 (from $275) while maintaining Outperform; UBS trimmed 2028E EPS to $18.80 and PT to $220 (from $240).

bullets.title: NVDA halts H200 shipments to China; zero China DC compute assumed in Q4 guidance
bullets.body: NVDA stopped shipping Hopper/H200 chips to China following tightened export controls; China datacenter compute revenue was $2.4B in Q3 and is assumed at zero for Q4. The board established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. Separately, NVDA is alleged to have introduced Alibaba to an alleged spy prior to 2022 export controls to find workarounds.

bullets.title: Hedge funds in fastest Info Tech net-selling pace in a decade; L/S leverage at 5-year lows
bullets.body: Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 7.6 pts MTD to below Liberation Day lows, the lowest in 5+ years. Info Tech experienced its fastest selling pace in 10 years (-4.4 z-score) over the past 6 weeks, with Semis & Semi Equipment leading; US Semis exposure has fallen below Software for the first time since early 2026. GS noted the global Info Tech long/short ratio dropped to 1.79 from a YTD peak of 2.9. The extreme positioning decline historically sets up tactical rally conditions as seasonality improves.

bullets.title: S&P closed below 200-dma for 4th straight down session; breadth 6:1 negative Tuesday
bullets.body: The SPX closed below its 200-day moving average Tuesday with decliners outnumbering advancers 6:1 and all 11 sectors lower; the Russell 2000 underperformed by 0.5%, down 1.5%. S&P futures are +0.13-0.2% and Nasdaq 100 futures +0.5% Wednesday morning on the NVDA print. JPM maintains its SPX year-end target at 8,000.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex tracking +104% YoY in CY27; cloud backlog rises to $2.5T from $2T
bullets.body: UBS updated hyperscaler OCF forecasts to +54%/+34% YoY in 2027/28, reaching $1.38T/$1.85T. Cloud industry backlog grew to $2.5T from $2T in just three months. NVDA's supply commitment increase of >$100B for C2027 delivery—while C2028 commits were flat—reinforces strong 2027 conviction but raises questions about 2028 growth visibility.

bullets.title: US consumer spending running above speed limit; Fed may need to tighten further
bullets.body: Atlanta Fed GDPNow is tracking 4Q26 real GDP at 3.4%, well above ~2% potential. October retail sales came in at +0.2% m/m (beat +0.1% consensus) with the control category +0.6% (beat +0.3%); core retail sales are +7.5% YoY. 22V Research notes the consumer is running ~1.5 ppts above potential growth, risking additional Fed tightening or delayed cuts; cyclicals expected to outperform once inflation slows in 2027.

bullets.title: Eurozone inflation still building; JPM calls two more ECB hikes (Dec 2026, Mar 2027)
bullets.body: Headline eurozone CPI hit 4.0% in October with energy inflation surging to 21.0% (+2 ppts MoM). JP Morgan expects core CPI to rise to 2.7-2.8% by end-Q1 2027 and forecasts two additional ECB rate hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, with risks skewed toward more tightening.

bullets.title: UK Oct CPI undershoots BoE across the board; December hike odds reduced
bullets.body: UK headline CPI rose to 3.6% YoY (below BoE's 3.7% forecast), core held at 2.8% (below 2.9%), and services at 3.7% (below 3.9%). JPM maintains its call for the next BoE hike in February 2027, noting the data lower the probability of a December move.

bullets.title: Software sector selling off on AI displacement fears; IGV down 9.5% YTD, -8.2% m/m
bullets.body: The software/IGV selloff has accelerated (-8.24% m/m) with multiple compression driven by fears that AI agents will replace seats and erode pricing power. The Wolfe All-SaaS index trades at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales (down 3.6% WoW) while the All-Security index is at 8.1x (down 7.5% WoW). IGV has returned -9.5% YTD vs S&P 500 +10.5%.

bullets.title: NVDA valuation at multi-decade lows: 10.6x fwd PE, 40% discount to SPX
bullets.body: After a ~$2T market cap wipeout (largest ever for any company), NVDA trades at 10.6x 12-month forward PE—its lowest in 13 years and a 40% discount to the S&P 500, the widest relative discount in 24 years. The SPX itself has de-rated 20% (from 23x to 17.6x) over the past 12 months. Morgan Stanley's MS Alpha flags Global Staples have outperformed Tech by 40% in under two months, the fastest pace since the TMT bubble, and now trade at a record 60% PE premium to IT.

bullets.title: FCC Chinese transceiver ban advancing; would create AI datacenter buildout bottleneck
bullets.body: The Trump administration is pressing ahead with a ban on Chinese optical transceiver imports despite hyperscaler opposition; 60-65% of optical transceivers are currently sourced from China. Morgan Stanley warns a full ban could create bottlenecks in AI datacenter builds, and China could retaliate by restricting indium exports (~70% of global supply), limiting alternative suppliers.

bullets.title: Tech outage cluster (MSFT, FAA, JPM, AAPL) stirs market anxiety; White House sees no coordinated attack
bullets.body: A series of major tech outages—Microsoft 365 (affecting ~500M people), an FAA nationwide ground stop (~20K flights canceled), JPMorgan and United software issues, and Apple service disruptions including an NSA classified network—occurred over five days. White House officials stated there is no evidence of a coordinated or state-sponsored cyberattack, attributing speculation to 'Black October' vulnerability disclosures.

bullets.title: Waymo pulled from all US highways after California DMV freeway ban
bullets.body: California's DMV ordered Waymo off state freeways following two recent incidents, citing imminent hazard to public safety. Alphabet responded by temporarily suspending Waymo highway operations nationwide. GOOGL is up ~0.7% pre-market despite the news.

bullets.title: Fed's Barr flags AI as emerging systemic financial risk; banks mapping AI credit exposure
bullets.body: Fed Governor Barr (Nov 16 speech) characterized AI infrastructure as a systemic financial risk and noted the Fed is now mapping credit plumbing and counterparty links in the AI buildout. Separately, Wall Street banks are reported to be curtailing exposure to AI infrastructure debt and expect global earnings growth to slow in 2027 as AI capex expansion cools.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO expected to price above $80/share, above initial $70-78 range
bullets.body: Broad market commentary notes the Anthropic IPO is expected to price above the initial $70-78 range, with headlines suggesting a price exceeding $80/share. The listing is cited as a focal point for the broader AI trade.

bullets.title: Memory becoming AI bottleneck; supply tightness expected through 2027-28
bullets.body: RBC and UBS both flag memory as the key gating factor for agentic AI deployment going forward. HBM wafer capacity is expected to grow from 390K to 690K WPM by end-2027; DRAM is forecast to remain undersupplied until Q2 2028 and NAND until Q4 2027. MU is highlighted as a preferred name with 100% excess cash return via buybacks planned.

bullets.title: Retail earnings: TGT, TJX beat; LOW comps strong but 4Q margin guide disappoints
bullets.body: TGT Q3 comps +5.6% (beat ~5% bar), gross margin 29.4% beat, traffic +5%; raised FY26 revenue guidance to 6% and EPS midpoint to ~$8.90 ex-refunds. TJX Q3 comps +4% vs +3% expectation; raised FY comps to 4% and buyback to ~$3B. LOW comps +1.8% (best since Q3 2022) but underlying gross margin compressed >230 bps ex-tariff refunds; implied Q4 EPS ~$1.72 vs consensus ~$1.97. Tariff refunds are materially distorting reported EPS across all three names.

bullets.title: NVDA stock at ~10x de-risked FY28 EPS; street split on whether CEO overhang is clearing event
bullets.body: With NVDA trading at ~10x FY28 consensus EPS (vs. a 5-year avg ~30x P/E), Morgan Stanley upgraded to Outperform with a $260 PT (+67% upside) and Citi raised its PT to $225 (maintaining 14x multiple vs prior 15x). However, Jefferies cut to $250, Wolfe cut to $200, and Summit Insights downgraded to Hold, citing CEO uncertainty, C2028 demand visibility, and export control risks. The investor survey from Citi showed 60% are selling NVDA, 85% buying NVDA competitors, and 90% buying NVDA suppliers.

bullets.title: NVDA neocloud financing stance turns more 'disciplined and selective'; $32B total commitments
bullets.body: NVDA's total neocloud guarantees stand at $32B (down from $36B QoQ) with $118B maximum guarantee exposure (including $105B SB Energy credit support). Management language on neocloud support shifted notably to 'disciplined and selective,' suggesting moderated growth for some neocloud operators. Citi investor survey shows 60% are net sellers of neocloud operators following the print.
